title: Geometric connectedness is tested by finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Then $Y$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if for every field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] that is finite ($\dim_kk'<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] the base change $Y_{k'}=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: ($\Rightarrow$) If $Y$ is geometrically connected over $k$, then by definition $Y_{k'}$ is connected for every field extension $k'/k$, in particular for every finite separable one.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, first sentence (line 950)

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), setup. Assume $Y_{k'}$ is connected for every finite separable $k'/k$ and, for a contradiction, that $Y$ is not geometrically connected. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois](1) choose a separable algebraic closure $\bar k/k$: $\bar k$ is separably closed and separable algebraic over $k$; by (2) it is Galois over $k$ and over every intermediate field. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ write $\sigma_Y=\mathrm{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$, the automorphism of $Y_{\bar k}$ given by base change [def-pc-base-change]; $(\sigma\circ\tau)_Y=\tau_Y\circ\sigma_Y$, $(\sigma^{-1})_Y=\sigma_Y^{-1}$, so each $\sigma_Y$ is a homeomorphism of $Y_{\bar k}$. Let $p:Y_{\bar k}\to Y$ be the projection; since $\sigma$ is a $k$-algebra map, $p\circ\sigma_Y=p$, hence $\sigma_Y(p^{-1}(S))=p^{-1}(S)$ for every subset $S\subseteq Y$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a map of one-point spaces, hence surjective, so $p$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, lines 951--953, and the action (equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar), lines 850--874

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), $Y$ is nonempty. Taking $k'=k$ (finite of degree one, and separable algebraic since each $a\in k$ has minimal polynomial $T-a$), $Y_k$ is connected, hence nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]; the projection $Y_k\to Y$ is an isomorphism (base change along the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}k$), so $Y\neq\emptyset$, and $Y_{\bar k}\ne\emptyset$ because $p$ is surjective.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020 (the case of empty $Y$, which the source passes over)

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), $Y_{\bar k}$ is disconnected (Stacks Lemma 0387). If $Y_{\bar k}$ were connected, then, $\bar k$ being separably closed, [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected] applied to the $\bar k$-scheme $Y_{\bar k}$ would make $Y_{\bar k}$ geometrically connected over $\bar k$, and [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension] applied to $\bar k/k$ would make $Y$ geometrically connected over $k$, contrary to the assumption. So $Y_{\bar k}$, which is nonempty by the previous step, is not connected: $Y_{\bar k}=\bar U\amalg\bar V$ with $\bar U,\bar V$ open, closed and nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, lines 953--958, citing Lemma Tag 0387 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected, lines 791--808), whose proof uses Lemma Tag 0363 and Lemma Tag 054N

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), quasi-compact pieces. Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open subset and $W_{\bar k}:=p^{-1}(W)$. Then $W_{\bar k}$ is open and quasi-compact: $W$ is a finite union of affine opens $W_i$, $p$ is quasi-compact as a base change of the quasi-compact morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a morphism of affine schemes) [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1),(3), so each $p^{-1}(W_i)$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a finite union of quasi-compact sets is quasi-compact. By the setup, $\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k})=W_{\bar k}$ for all $\sigma$. The sets $W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U$ and $W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V$ are open in $Y_{\bar k}$, complementary in $W_{\bar k}$, and closed in the quasi-compact space $W_{\bar k}$, hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-galois-base-change-qc-open-descends](2), applied to $V=W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U$, there is a finite subextension $k\subseteq k_W\subseteq\bar k$ with $\rho_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)=W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U$ for all $\rho\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k_W)$; then also $\rho_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V)=W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V$, the complement in the invariant set $W_{\bar k}$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, second paragraph (lines 959--970), using Lemma Tag 04KU

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), choice of $k'$. Pick $u\in\bar U$ and an affine open $W_0\subseteq Y$ containing $p(u)$; it is quasi-compact and $W_{0,\bar k}\cap\bar U\ni u$ is nonempty. Let $k':=k_{W_0}$ be the finite subextension of the previous step for $W_0$ and $H:=\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k')$, a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$; thus $\sigma_Y(W_{0,\bar k}\cap\bar U)=W_{0,\bar k}\cap\bar U$ for $\sigma\in H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois](2), $k'/k$ is separable algebraic, and it is finite by construction.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, third paragraph (lines 971--983)

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), finiteness of the $H$-translates. Let $W$ be a quasi-compact open of $Y$ and $A:=W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U$, with $k_W$ as above. If $\sigma,\tau\in H$ and $\sigma^{-1},\tau^{-1}$ agree on $k_W$, then $\rho:=\tau\circ\sigma^{-1}$ fixes $k_W$ pointwise (for $x\in k_W$: $\rho(x)=\tau(\sigma^{-1}(x))=\tau(\tau^{-1}(x))=x$), and $\tau=\rho\circ\sigma$ gives $\tau_Y(A)=\sigma_Y(\rho_Y(A))=\sigma_Y(A)$. The restrictions $\sigma^{-1}|_{k_W}$ are $k$-algebra homomorphisms $k_W\to\bar k$, of which there are finitely many since $\dim_kk_W<\infty$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-finitely-many-embeddings]. Hence $\{\sigma_Y(A):\sigma\in H\}$ and likewise $\{\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V):\sigma\in H\}$ are finite families. (The source phrases this as invariance under an open subgroup of the profinite Galois group.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, fourth paragraph (lines 985--996: 'the union and intersection above are finite')

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), the sets $U_W,V_W$. For a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Y$ put $U_W:=\bigcap_{\sigma\in H}\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)$ and $V_W:=\bigcup_{\sigma\in H}\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V)$. Since $\sigma_Y$ is a homeomorphism fixing $W_{\bar k}$, $\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)$ and $\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V)$ are complementary open and closed subsets of $W_{\bar k}$; by the previous step the intersection and the union are finite, so $U_W$ and $V_W=W_{\bar k}\setminus U_W$ are open and closed in $W_{\bar k}$, hence open in $Y_{\bar k}$, and $W_{\bar k}=U_W\amalg V_W$. For $\tau\in H$, $\tau_Y(U_W)=\bigcap_\sigma(\sigma\circ\tau)_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)=U_W$ because $\sigma\mapsto\sigma\circ\tau$ is a bijection of $H$; likewise $\tau_Y(V_W)=V_W$. Since $W_{0,\bar k}\cap\bar U$ is $H$-invariant, $U_{W_0}=W_{0,\bar k}\cap\bar U\neq\emptyset$; and $V_W\supseteq W_{\bar k}\cap\bar V$ ($\sigma=\mathrm{id}$).

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, fourth paragraph (lines 985--998)

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), compatibility (the source's 'verification omitted'). If $W\subseteq W'$ are quasi-compact opens, then $W_{\bar k}\subseteq W'_{\bar k}$ and, as $\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k})=W_{\bar k}$ and $\sigma_Y$ is bijective, $W_{\bar k}\cap\sigma_Y(W'_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)=\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap W'_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)=\sigma_Y(W_{\bar k}\cap\bar U)$; intersecting over $\sigma\in H$ gives $W_{\bar k}\cap U_{W'}=U_W$, and the same computation with unions gives $W_{\bar k}\cap V_{W'}=V_W$. Consequently, for any two quasi-compact opens $W,W'$ (so $W\cup W'$ is quasi-compact open), $U_W\cap W'_{\bar k}=U_{W\cup W'}\cap W_{\bar k}\cap W'_{\bar k}\subseteq U_{W\cup W'}\cap W'_{\bar k}=U_{W'}$, and similarly for $V$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0389 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected), proof, lines 948--1020, fifth paragraph (lines 1004--1012)

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$), descent to $k'$ and contradiction. Let $q:Y_{\bar k}\to Y_{k'}$ be $\mathrm{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}(k'\hookrightarrow\bar k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] (pasting the cartesian squares of $Y_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$), $(Y_{\bar k},q,\mathrm{pr})$ is the base change of the $k'$-scheme $Y_{k'}$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$, and for $\sigma\in H=\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k')$ the automorphism $\mathrm{id}_{Y_{k'}}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ equals $\sigma_Y$ (both have the same compositions with the two projections, by the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]). As $\bar k/k'$ is Galois [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois](2) and $U,V$ are closed and $H$-invariant, [lem-weil-pbc-galois-invariant-closed-subset-descends] (for the field $k'$, the $k'$-scheme $Y_{k'}$ and $\bar k/k'$) gives closed $U',V'\subseteq Y_{k'}$ with $q^{-1}(U')=U$, $q^{-1}(V')=V$. The morphism $q$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] (base change of the surjection of one-point spaces $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$). Hence $U'\cup V'=Y_{k'}$ (each point has a preimage, lying in $U$ or $V$), $U'\cap V'=\emptyset$ (a common point would have a preimage in $U\cap V$), and $U'=q(U)$, $V'=q(V)$ are nonempty. So $Y_{k'}$ is the disjoint union of two nonempty closed, hence open and closed, subsets and is not connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], although $k'/k$ is finite and separable algebraic (setup of $k'$). This contradiction proves that $Y$ is geometrically connected.
